comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
There's a time and place. The warm tint itself is not a hallmark of low quality, or else games like Stardew Valley would never have been successful. And it's a fairly common aesthetic for old games, and VERY common for stills due to portrait and landscape painters  loving Golden Hour (for good reason). If it's applied inconsistently, that's a different story.

It  frustrates me when people come to dislike something due to prevalence, when it itself is not a bad thing. I've heard people talk trash about Ghibli in the last year because of all the Ghiblifying people were doing with  AI, as if the art style itself was bad. It's a really stupid take, frankly, and reminds me of people who hate music just because it becomes popular. Getting tired of something is different from it being strictly bad.

I say this as someone who leans flat color/cel-shaded in my own art style, so not exactly something I have to contend with personally.
